items.followUp: A crane lifts a 150 kg load through 8 m in 12 s. Calculate its power, taking g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The student identifies power as work done per unit time.
rubric.how: Award for stating power equals work divided by time.

rubric.why: The work calculation must use the load’s weight and the vertical height lifted.
rubric.how: Award for substituting the given values with g = 10 m s⁻² and obtaining work = 12000 J. Accept a consistent calculation using g = 9.8 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The final result is power, expressed in watts.
rubric.how: Award for 1200 W using g = 10 m s⁻², or 1176 W using g = 9.8 m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: m = 200 kg, h = 6 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m s⁻²
Power, P = work done / time = mgh / t
The power of the pump is 1200 W.

rubric.why: Mechanics is defined by the physical topics it studies.
rubric.how: Award for identifying mechanics as the branch of physics dealing with motion and forces.

rubric.why: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award for stating that heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body.

modelAnswer: Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.
Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body because of a temperature difference.

items.followUp: A person walks 120 m east in 20 s. Find their velocity.

rubric.why: Velocity describes how displacement changes with time.
rubric.how: Award for defining velocity as the rate of change of displacement.

rubric.why: Acceleration describes how velocity changes with time.
rubric.how: Award for defining acceleration as the rate of change of velocity.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

items.followUp: Can a car moving at constant speed around a circular track be accelerating? Explain.

rubric.why: The answer must recognise that acceleration can occur even when speed is constant.
A change in direction changes velocity and therefore produces acceleration.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the changing direction changes velocity, so the body is accelerating.

modelAnswer: Yes, a body moving at constant speed can have acceleration.
If its direction changes, its velocity changes; therefore it is accelerating.

items.followUp: What is plasma? State one property of it.

rubric.why: Plasma is identified as the fourth state of matter.
Plasma is a gas containing charged particles.
rubric.how: Award for describing it as an ionized gas containing positive ions and free electrons.

modelAnswer: The fourth state of matter is plasma.
Plasma is an ionized gas consisting of positive ions and free electrons.

items.followUp: Define specific heat capacity and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Heat capacity is defined by the heat needed for a one-degree temperature rise of the whole body.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the heat required to raise the temperature of a body by 1 K (or 1 °C).

rubric.why: The SI unit expresses heat energy per temperature rise.
rubric.how: Award for J K⁻¹ (joule per kelvin).

modelAnswer: Heat capacity is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a body by 1 K.
Its SI unit is J K⁻¹.

items.followUp: State two properties of a good thermometric substance.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion makes temperature readings consistent.
rubric.how: Award for stating that mercury expands uniformly with temperature.

rubric.why: Any further suitable property explains why mercury is useful in thermometers.
rubric.how: Award for one additional valid reason, such as being shiny and easily visible, having a wide liquid-temperature range, not wetting glass, high thermal conductivity, or low specific heat.

modelAnswer: Mercury expands uniformly when its temperature changes, giving a reliable temperature scale.
It is shiny and easily visible in the thermometer tube.
It remains liquid over a wide range of temperatures and does not wet the glass.

items.followUp: Convert 5 nm per day into mm s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The nanometre and day must be converted to the requested units.
rubric.how: Award for using 1 nm = 10⁻⁶ mm and 1 day = 86400 s.

rubric.why: The final rate must be in millimetres per second.
rubric.how: Award for 1.16 × 10⁻¹¹ mm s⁻¹ (or an equivalent rounded value).

modelAnswer: Given: growth = 1 nm day⁻¹
1 nm = 10⁻⁶ mm; 1 day = 86400 s
Growth rate = (10⁻⁶ mm) / (86400 s)
Growth rate = 1.16 × 10⁻¹¹ mm s⁻¹
